title: $18 an Hour Is How Much a Year? (2026)
metaDescription: $18/hour is $37,440 a year at 40 hrs/week — $3,120 monthly, $1,440.00 biweekly. See overtime pay tables and a 2026 federal take-home estimate.

hero.lede: Full time at 40 hours a week, 52 weeks a year (2,080 hours). Below: every pay-period equivalent, overtime tables at time-and-a-half, and a 2026 federal-only take-home estimate.

shortAnswer.heading: How much is $18 an hour per year?
shortAnswer.html: $18 an hour is $37,440 a year at 40 hours a week for 52 weeks (2,080 hours). That's $720.00 a week, $1,440.00 biweekly, and $3,120.00 a month gross. After estimated federal income tax and FICA, a single filer keeps about $32,263 — and steady overtime at $27.00/hour raises the total fast.

sections.title: What $18/hour adds up to per period.
sections.note: Gross (pre-tax) figures assuming paid hours every week of the year. Unpaid time off reduces them proportionally.

sections.title: $18 an hour in 2026, in plain numbers.
paragraphs: At $18 an hour, a full-time year — 40 hours a week for 52 weeks, with no unpaid time off — grosses $37,440. That's $720.00 a week, $1,440.00 per biweekly paycheck, and about $3,120.00 a month before taxes.

Measured against the middle of the U.S. labor market, $18/hour is about 42% below the U.S. median full-time wage — the BLS median works out to about $31.28/hour ($1,251/week, BLS, Q2 2026). The big lever for hourly earners is overtime: every OT hour pays $27.00 at time-and-a-half.

sections.title: Overtime at $27.00/hour changes the math quickly.
sections.note: Overtime rows assume time-and-a-half (1.5 × $18 = $27.00) on hours past 40, every week of the year — the FLSA baseline for non-exempt workers.

sections.title: From $37,440 gross to take-home.
sections.note: Single filer, standard deduction, no state/local income tax, credits, or pre-tax benefits. Actual checks vary.

sections.title: What a single filer actually keeps.
paragraphs: Federally, this wage puts a single filer in the 12% marginal bracket for 2026: $37,440 gross less the $16,100 standard deduction is $21,340 taxable, generating $2,313 of income tax (6.2% effective). Add $2,864 of FICA and estimated take-home is $32,263/year, or $2,688.59/month.

faq.q: How much is $18 an hour per year?
faq.a: $18 an hour is $37,440 a year at full time — 40 hours a week for 52 weeks (2,080 hours). At 30 hours a week it comes to $28,080, and with 10 hours of weekly overtime it reaches about $51,480.

faq.q: How much is $18 an hour biweekly?
faq.a: A standard 80-hour biweekly period at $18/hour grosses $1,440.00. After estimated federal income tax and FICA for a single filer, roughly $1,240.89 remains per check, before state taxes.

faq.q: How much is $18 an hour after taxes?
faq.a: On $37,440 of annual wages, a single filer taking the 2026 standard deduction pays about $2,313 of federal income tax plus $2,864 of FICA, keeping roughly $32,263 a year — about $15.51 per hour worked. State and local taxes reduce this further where they apply.

faq.q: How much is $18 an hour with overtime?
faq.a: Overtime pays time-and-a-half: $27.00 per hour past 40 in a week. A steady 50-hour week earns $990.00 weekly — $51,480 a year, $14,040 more than the straight 40-hour year.

faq.q: Is $18 an hour a good wage in 2026?
faq.a: $18/hour annualizes to $37,440, which is about 42% below the U.S. median full-time wage — the BLS median for full-time workers is $1,251/week (about $31.28/hour, BLS, Q2 2026). Local cost of living, benefits, and schedule stability matter as much as the rate itself.

methodology: Annualization is straight arithmetic: $18 × 2,080 hours (40 hours × 52 weeks) = $37,440, with daily/weekly/biweekly/monthly rows derived the same way. No unpaid leave is assumed.
Overtime rows use the FLSA non-exempt baseline of 1.5× base pay ($27.00/hour) on hours over 40 per week, sustained all 52 weeks.
The take-home estimate uses 2026 federal brackets for a single filer with the $16,100 standard deduction plus employee FICA (7.65%). It excludes state/local tax, credits, and pre-tax benefits.
Median-wage comparison: BLS median usual weekly earnings, full-time workers, $1,251/week (BLS, Q2 2026).
